meta_description: High-Performance & Mission-Critical Systems from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: High-Performance & Mission-Critical Systems as delivered by Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, the platforms involved and the outcomes we commit to at each gate.

Some systems are the product: matching and pricing engines, grid-adjacent control workloads, real-time bidding, high-throughput risk calculation. We engineer for their physics — latency budgets broken down per hop, kernel-bypass and FPGA accelerators where justified, NUMA-aware placement, and determinism testing under adversarial load. Availability engineering pairs with it: active-active topologies, chaos-verified failover, and capacity headroom policies tied to revenue risk.

HPC workloads (simulation, risk grids, genomic pipelines, CFD) get the same discipline on clusters: scheduler tuning, GPU partitioning, storage tiering for burst patterns, and reproducible environments via containers. Every mission-critical build ships with a load-and-failure evidence pack — the numbers that let the business sign off on what 'always on' actually means.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
